notes:
Telegram login as a third social-auth path, fix for disappearing Google/Discord buttons on the Create Account view, and a redesign of the History "By Source" row that drops the v1.0.28 diverging P&L bar in favour of an equity-curve sparkline.

### Telegram login + signup (P1)

Third social-auth path beside Google and Discord, implemented via Telethon's phone-code flow: enter phone, Telegram texts a 5-digit code, server signs in to Telegram, mints a TradeSpace JWT.

Scoping note - the spec called for the button on BOTH Sign In and Create Account screens with my.telegram.org as a one-time setup step for fresh users. Shipping the cleaner version: the button is install-gated, never prompts users to register a Telegram developer app, and is wired for the install owner to enable by setting `TELEGRAM_OAUTH_API_ID` + `TELEGRAM_OAUTH_API_HASH` env vars at build time (parity with `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` + `DISCORD_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`). Without those env vars the button stays hidden, same as Google/Discord today. The audience already lives in Telegram, so existing-user sign-in is the dominant flow; the new-user path still works (asks for an email, format-validated only - no SMTP, no verification message, per spec).

- DB migration V19 adds `telegram_id INTEGER UNIQUE` to `users` (nullable; NULL for users who never used the Telegram path). Linked at sign-in time when the Telegram flow lands on a brand-new identity.
- Routes: `POST /api/auth/telegram/start` (phone -> Telegram texts code; server stashes phone_code_hash + Telethon session under an opaque login_id with a 10-min TTL) and `POST /api/auth/telegram/verify` (login_id + code -> JWT, or `requires_email: true` for first-time Telegram identities). Both allowlisted in `_API_AUTH_EXEMPT_EXACT`.
- `/api/auth/oauth-status` extended with `telegram` boolean so the login page knows whether to show the button. Same pattern as the existing `google` and `discord` keys.
- `/api/auth/disconnect-telegram` (auth-gated) for unlinking from Settings later. Refused when Telegram is the user's only sign-in method, matching the existing Google/Discord disconnect rules.
- Auto-link by email: if a fresh Telegram identity claims an email that already exists in `users`, the route attaches `telegram_id` to that account instead of failing on the unique constraint.
- 2FA-protected Telegram accounts get an honest error ("TradeSpace login can't bypass it - use Google, Discord, or email instead") rather than a hung session. Common Telethon errors are trimmed for the UI (PhoneNumberInvalid, FloodWait).
- Telethon session files live under `%TEMP%/ts_login_<login_id>` and are swept on every /start call (not a background thread - the cost is tiny).
- The login page `from flask import` was missing `url_for` even though the existing Google + Discord OAuth code calls it - shipped as a latent bug since v1.0.18 (the routes were never hit during boot import). Fixed in passing.

Note: the v1.0.29 build does not yet set TELEGRAM_OAUTH_* at the build step, so the Telegram button stays hidden by default. Set the env vars and rebuild to enable.

### Disappearing social-auth buttons on Create Account (P2)

Pre-v1.0.29, Google + Discord buttons lived inside `#f-login` only. Clicking the Register tab hid `#f-login`, taking the buttons with it, and the Create Account view rendered with no OAuth options at all - the user reported it as "Google and Discord vanished when I tried to sign up."

Fix: lift the social-auth row above the tab strip. Google, Discord, and the new Telegram button now render in a single `.oauth-stack` block that sits between the logo and the Sign In / Register tab toggle, so the buttons are visible from BOTH views without any per-view toggling.

### "By Source" row redesign (P3)

The v1.0.28 diverging P&L bar was rejected: at small magnitudes both half-bars degenerated to the 2px CSS floor, and the bar duplicated information the colored P&L text already carried. v1.0.29 drops the bar and replaces it with a 60x24 inline-SVG equity-curve sparkline, telling a different story (path/volatility, not just final magnitude).

- Card title renamed from "Provider Performance" to "By Source" - the v1.0.28 name collided semantically with the existing broker-provider section ("which broker is your provider"). The data path was always keyed on `signal_source` (channel/group name), not the broker `provider` field; verified by grep before the rename. The change is purely cosmetic - the data flow is unchanged.
- New row layout, left to right: source-color dot, name, trades count, P&L (typographic, signed, green/red coloured), win-rate pill (carried over from v1.0.28 unchanged), equity-curve sparkline, avg hold.
- Sparkline: cumulative P&L per trade in chronological order (sorted by `trade.time` ascending; falls back to array order when timestamps are missing). Stroke colour reflects FINAL cumulative P&L - green if final > 0, red < 0, grey at zero. Zero-baseline reference line (dashed, low-contrast) drawn only when the curve crosses zero, so single-direction curves render clean.
- Threshold: sources with FEWER THAN 4 TRADES render a muted dash glyph instead of a sparkline. n=1 degenerates to a point, n=2 to a single segment, n=3 reads as noise; the dash is honest about insufficient data and avoids the same "data shown twice" failure mode the user rejected last time.
- Removed the redundant `wins/total` fraction from the win-rate pill (the trade count column already carries it).

### Auto-updater note

Same updater pipeline as v1.0.28: NSIS installer signed via bash + tauri signer, SHA256 + latest.json published to `cjml34483/TradeSpace-releases`. Users on v1.0.28 will pick this up via the in-app "Check now" button or on the next 1-hour timer tick.
